answer: A verifiable delay function makes each new agent identity cost real wall-clock time. To register, an agent must compute a long sequential puzzle that cannot be parallelized, and anyone can check the proof in milliseconds. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes cannot buy a faster shortcut; he must run a thousand machines for days, a slow trek across a dry mesa with no oasis. Identities also expire unless renewed, so the cost recurs, and honest agents, like yarrow, keep growing on one cheap root.
